items.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.7
items.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.7, a 2.1-trillion-parameter frontier model (up 40% from Grok 4.6) built on a larger base model and a longer reinforcement-learning run, with improved self-verification and a 500K-token context window. It targets coding and agentic professional workflows and is available via the Grok API, Cursor and Grok Build at the same price as its predecessor.

items.headline: Meta's Muse AI assistant tops US app charts with 900,000+ downloads in six days
items.summary: Meta's new consumer AI agent, Muse, rocketed to the top of mobile app charts with strong early reviews, signaling real traction in the crowded consumer AI-assistant market ahead of Meta's Connect keynote.

items.headline: Meta's AI agent Muse blocked from using Amazon.com
items.summary: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse AI shopping agent from operating on its site, the latest flashpoint in a broader clash between retailers and AI agents over who controls the checkout experience.

items.headline: Researchers used Claude to help breach OpenAI's internal systems in under 72 hours
items.summary: Three Hacktron security researchers used Anthropic's Claude to help design an exploit that accessed OpenAI employee session data and an internal repository as part of authorized research; OpenAI fixed the flaw within about 14 hours and paid a $6,500 bounty.

items.headline: SoftBank launches $11B+ bond sale to fund its OpenAI investment
items.summary: SoftBank Group is issuing $10B in dollar bonds plus €1B in euro notes, potentially the largest APAC non-financial corporate bond deal on record, to help fund a follow-on OpenAI investment expected to close next month.

items.headline: Trump presses the case for AI ahead of Xi meeting as slowdown calls rise
items.summary: The administration is pushing an aggressive pro-AI posture ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting, even as an industry-coordination antitrust lawsuit and warnings from AI pioneers add pressure for a policy course correction.

items.headline: Google DeepMind's 'Dream-RSI' lets AI agents self-improve by replaying imagined searches
items.summary: A new paper from Google DeepMind, University of Maryland and UVA researchers introduces Dream-RSI, which lets an agent improve its own search strategy by replaying imagined variations of past attempts against a simulator, with no retraining needed. It cuts discovery-agent calls up to 162x versus the prior baseline across algorithm engineering, math optimization and GPU kernel tasks.

items.headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue projected to top $100 billion in 2026 ahead of Nasdaq IPO
items.summary: Anthropic is on track to exceed $100 billion in annualized revenue this year as it prepares for a trading debut as soon as November, having chosen Nasdaq for its listing.

items.headline: D-Robotics raises $400M Series C for humanoid and industrial robot chips
items.summary: Chinese chipmaker D-Robotics closed a $400M Series C led by Mirae Asset, bringing total funding to roughly $770M, to expand its Sunrise chip line (8M+ units shipped) for humanoid and industrial robots — described as China's largest robotics funding deal in four years.

items.headline: Chinese 'robot brain' startup Spirit AI predicts a ChatGPT-style breakthrough for humanoids by 2027
items.summary: Embodied-AI startup Spirit AI says a breakthrough in general-purpose robot intelligence comparable to GPT-3's impact on language models could arrive as soon as mid-2027; the company says its Moz1 robots already hit roughly 90% success rates on simple structured tasks and are deployed at CATL and JD.com facilities.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches institute to widen the AGI debate
items.summary: DeepMind launched a new institute aimed at broadening discussion of artificial general intelligence beyond Silicon Valley insiders, alongside its parallel proposal for an independent frontier-AI standards body.

items.headline: Cohere and Aleph Alpha sign definitive $20 billion merger agreement
items.summary: The two companies formalized a combination first disclosed in April, creating a dual-headquartered (Berlin/Toronto) roughly $20 billion entity operating under the Cohere name, positioned as a transatlantic rival to OpenAI and Anthropic; the deal awaits regulatory approval.

items.headline: 'Godfather of AI' Yoshua Bengio says AI regulation is nearing a Covid-style pivot moment
items.summary: Bengio said governments may be approaching a rapid-response turning point on AI regulation similar to early Covid-19 policy shifts, citing recent safety incidents as evidence that public and government concern is accelerating.
